Battle of Enderta was a clash between Özdemiroğlu Osman Pasha and the Ethiopian King Menas.
Battle
In July 1561, King Menas defeated Yeshaq in a battle at Wagara. Yeshak retreated to Massawa and sought Ottoman refuge. Osman Pasha made significant use of him during his campaigns in Ethiopia. Indeed, Debrav and its surrounding area fell to the Ottomans in January 1562. Osman Pasha then inflicted a devastating defeat on Menas at Enderta in the southern territories on April 20, 1562. Despite Menas's superior army, Ottoman firearms decided the outcome of this battle. The roar of the Ottoman cannons struck terror into the Ethiopian army, so much so that Menas’s soldiers often abandoned the battlefield without fighting.
